changes.before: Open only the second output stream with std::ios::app. What text is read after both writes succeed?
changes.after: Write a file, check for failure, and read its text back.

before: This example creates or overwrites practice.txt in the current working directory. Run it only in a disposable folder; the test harness supplies one. Existing personal files are never needed.
An ofstream opened this way truncates an existing file. std::ios::app instead writes at the end. Neither insertion of a string nor opening in append mode adds a newline automatically.

if(!out) checks stream failure. Explicit close followed by a state check can detect a failed final write; destruction still closes resources through RAII, but does not report successful persistence to the caller. ifstream and getline also need success checks.

std::ifstream in("practice.txt") opens that file for input. std::getline(in, text) reads into text until a newline or end-of-file; it consumes a found newline without storing it. Its returned stream can be tested for success before using text.
Expected output or behavior: second. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Try explicit newlines and read all lines in a loop; keep the file inside a disposable folder. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: A file stream connects the program to a file. std::ofstream writes, and std::ifstream reads. This example creates or overwrites practice.txt in the current folder. Run it in a disposable practice folder without a file you need to keep.
Opening ofstream this way clears an existing file before writing. std::ios::app would instead append, meaning add at the end. Writing text does not add a newline unless the text includes one.

if (!out) detects stream failure. Checking after close() can catch a failed final write. RAII still closes streams during destruction, but automatic cleanup alone does not confirm that writing succeeded.
When the operations succeed, the program prints second. The second output stream clears the earlier contents before writing its own text.

std::getline(in, text) reads up to a newline or the end of the file. It removes a found newline from the input without storing it in text. The returned stream is checked before the program prints the result.

before.question: Open only the second output stream with std::ios::app. What text is read after both writes succeed?
choices: first followed by an automatic newline and second
before.explanation: Appending preserves first and adds the exact characters second. Neither write supplied a newline.

after.question: Open only the second output stream with std::ios::app. After successful writes, what text is read?
choices: first, then an automatically added newline, then second
after.explanation: Appending keeps first and adds second directly after it. Neither write supplies a newline.
